items.reason: Identifies the missing prisma import in Salesforce's new credential update.
Includes the unconditional Salesforce token refresh and database write on every service construction, without an expiry check.
Identifies the computed Zod keys being literal property names rather than wildcards, breaking sync-mode token validation.
Identifies the fabricated refresh_token placeholder overwriting a valid stored refresh token.
Identifies Google Calendar persisting the SafeParse wrapper instead of its token data.
Identifies the raw fetch Response returned in sync mode being incompatible with callers' expected provider-specific shapes.
Reports the same sync-response shape mismatch at the Zoho Bigin caller, which expects an axios-style data property.
Identifies Office365's now-unreachable failure check and lost error logging because the parser throws on invalid data.
Identifies the webhook secret's non-constant-time string comparison.
Identifies Zoho Bigin passing the credential row id where refreshOAuthTokens requires the owning user's id.
Identifies the SafeParse wrapper being stored as Google's credential key instead of the parsed data.
Identifies the credential id incorrectly being sent as calcomUserId by Zoho Bigin.
Identifies timing leakage from the webhook secret's direct string comparison.
Reports the empty-string fallback for a missing encryption key. This is distinct from the golden issue about unhandled payload validation and decryption errors; fixing either does not fix the other.
Identifies Google storing the SafeParse result wrapper rather than its credential data.
Identifies Zoho Bigin supplying credentialId instead of userId to the sync helper.
Identifies the SafeParse wrapper corrupting the persisted Google credential structure.
Identifies the credential row id incorrectly used as the Cal.com user id in Zoho Bigin's refresh call.
Identifies the raw fetch Response lacking the data property expected by Google and Zoho refresh callers.
Identifies Google persisting the SafeParse wrapper as credential.key, breaking subsequent credential parsing.
Primarily identifies and proposes fixing Zoho Bigin's credentialId/userId mix-up. It also mentions the separate response-shape mismatch covered by issue #09.
Identifies computed Zod keys creating literal required properties instead of validating arbitrary token fields.
Identifies the literal refresh_token placeholder overwriting valid stored refresh tokens when the response omits that field.
